text:
morgan: kicking off APAC GPU region onboarding thread. goal: proposal for terraform module layout + pulumi stack wiring + CI changes so SRE can handoff to region owners. looking for quick reviews and any hard constraints (quotas, net limits, billing tags).

lee: SGTM. which clouds/instance types are we targeting? H100 availability varies by zone.

morgan: primary target is GCP -> a2-highgpu-1g and hpc-ish H100 where available. fallback to A100 (a2) in zones without H100. we need terraform to expose a "gpu_profile" var and a simple compatibility map. also need a quota check job in CI to fail early.

anya: adding quota check makes sense. we already have a small GH Action in infra-shared that calls GCP quota API. can reuse. :+1:

sam: quick note on networking: we should avoid VPC peering across prod/regional VPCs; prefer Shared VPC + subnet ranges allocated in advance. APAC has limited /22 ranges available, need to reserve.

morgan: noted. planning doc snippet:

```
module "apac_region" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/region-modules.git//gcp-region?ref=main"

  region            = "asia-southeast2"
  project_id        = "redwood-apac-prod"
  gpu_profile       = var.gpu_profile
  shared_vpc        = true
  subnet_range      = "10.64.0.0/22"
  remote_state      = {
    backend = "gcs"
    bucket  = "redwood-terraform-state-apac"
    prefix  = "apac/asia-southeast2"
    lock    = "gcs-locking"
  }
}
```

lee: couple caveats:
- GCS backend + object versioning is fine but locking requires either `gcloud alpha` style or a separate CloudSQL/Datastore lock table if we want cross-team safety. Pulumi already supports state locking with GCS? we usually use `gsutil` + lock file in bucket for TF.
- Need a lifecycle rule to auto-delete old tfstate backups (compliance allows 90 days).

anya: for Pulumi stacks we should mirror the TF layout but keep Pulumi stacks per team. recommend stack naming: `apac-prod-<team>` and use service account impersonation. in CI, add `PULUMI_LOGIN` to GH secrets and use ephemeral key creation flow.

morgan: here's the proposed GH Action snippet for TF plan + quota check + backends:

```
name: apac-region-provision
on: [workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  check-quotas:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: quota check
        run: scripts/check_gcp_quotas.sh asia-southeast2 a2_family
  terraform:
    needs: check-quotas
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: init
        run: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-terraform-state-apac" -backend-config="prefix=apac/asia-southeast2"
      - name: plan
        run: terraform plan -var="gpu_profile=${{ inputs.gpu_profile }}"
```

natalie: for handoff checklist, add cost-watch and pre-provision alerting. APAC egress costs can be surprising if control plane cross-region traffic happens. Also add expected instance hourly cost estimates to PR.

morgan: good call. i'll add a cost table. rough numbers: H100 ~ $12/hr, A100 ~ $6.5/hr (ballpark depending on zone). include spot vs on-demand recommendations.

sam: also confirm image compatibility: some H100 images require specific drivers and TF nodetypes (NVIDIA driver > 525). add a node-init script in module.

lee: about state wiring: i propose we keep TF state in a dedicated GCS bucket per region with object locking + IAM bindings: only `infra-ci` SA and `infra-admins` group can write. Pulumi state should be in Pulumi Service for hosted stacks for now to avoid duplicating locking logic.

morgan: decision point: Pulumi hosted vs self-managed state. Hosted gives us easier stack history and locking but is enterprise plan. For now, teams that need private should opt into `pulumi self-host` pattern. i'll add that to the docs.

infra-bot: reminder: create a CloudBilling alert for project `redwood-apac-prod` - threshold $500/day for first 7 days.

anya: picked up infra-bot. also: onboarding runbook draft - minimal steps for handoff: 1) create TF PR with module + vars 2) run quota check CI 3) run `terraform apply` in infra-admin account 4) create pulumi stack for team and transfer SA 5) verify GPU nodes register and run stress test 6) tag resources with billing tags 7) close handoff ticket.

morgan: adding verification commands:
```
# check node GPU health
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
# check driver on node
ssh core@<node-ip> 'nvidia-smi'
# run basic perf test
kubectl run perf --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:latest --restart=Never -- nvidia-smi
```

sam: can we add a tiny e2e CI that deploys a small inference replica to validate model loading? maybe pull a 1GB model and load to ensure KV cache path works.

morgan: yes — add a `smoke/inference-load` GH action that runs after provisioning. will need a test dataset and budget cap.

lee: one more networking thing: ensure default route priority doesn't leak traffic to prod/global NAT. use regional NATs and set `cloud_router` with advertised IPs.

morgan: will do. final ask: can ppl review the module layout in PR #512 (link: https://github.com/redwood-infra/region-modules/pull/512) and mark approvals or post blockers here? plan to merge by EOD Friday if no blockers.

anya: reviewing now.

sam: quick look, left 2 comments on subnet allocation and SA roles.

natalie: approved pending cost table and billing alert.

morgan: thanks all. if no other blockers i’ll merge after addressing comments. :rocket:
